body:
Supersession takes effect at the queue's next transform cycle, not retroactively

## Decision

A document that supersedes *after* one submit cycle's queue read but *before*
its batch collects is not retroactively retired from an in-flight
reservation. The queue is a point-in-time FULL snapshot, read once per
submit; retiring an already-submitted batch line would need to reach into a
pending provider batch mid-flight, which batch APIs do not support.

## Why

Supersession takes effect at the queue's *next* transform cycle, which
naturally re-scopes the due-list. Given batches run on an hours-not-days
scale and the queue rebuilds every cycle, this is a bounded, self-healing
staleness window rather than a correctness gap — no compensating action is
needed.
lead: Supersession takes effect at the queue's next transform cycle, not retroactively
title: Mid-cycle document supersession does not retire an in-flight batch reservation
